gap: No result ChatGPT got states the measured no-load inverter draw of each candidate (HOBOTECH 85 W Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus, 52 W EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra; The Solar Lab ~80 W Anker F3800, 36 W DELTA Pro Ultra X, ~20 W BLUETTI Apex 300; pv magazine ~10 W Anker SOLIX S5000). At a 40-50 W fan that overhead is as large as the fan itself, so the 5,024 Wh S5000 gives more fan nights (about 10) than the 6,144 Wh DELTA Pro Ultra (about 7), and the F3800 drops from ChatGPT's 8-10 nights to about 3.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Solar Waypoint F3800 vs DELTA Pro Ultra vs Jackery 5000 Plus comparison (rated Wh only, no measurements), RuntimeWise home-backup best list (says runtimes are calculated at a flat 85% and 'We haven't hands-on tested these units'), BackupPowerHub home-backup list (flat 0.85 factor, 'doesn't run lab tests', no idle figure) and EnoughWatts' power-station table (capacity, output, price only). GearSpec Outpost returned HTTP 429 twice, so it was not checked. Both ChatGPT answers rank by Wh × 85%. The second one says 'actual runtime may be lower due to idle inverter draw' but gives no number for any model.
decides: It changes the pick. Counting fan + measured idle for 8 h a night at 50 W: Anker SOLIX S5000 ≈ 10.1 nights (4,870 Wh delivered / 480 Wh a night), EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra ≈ 7.4 (about 6,021 Wh / 816), Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus ≈ 4.1 (4,450 / 1,080), BLUETTI Apex 300 ≈ 4.2 (about 2,350 / 560), Anker F3800 ≈ 2.9 (2,980 / 1,040). Among single base units, the S5000 (which Dealectric lists on Rakuten) runs a fan for the most nights, ahead of the larger DELTA Pro Ultra that ChatGPT picked. Only the two-battery DELTA Pro Ultra X (12,288 Wh, 36 W idle, about 15 nights on an assumed 85% usable) runs longer, at whole-home-system cost. The Apex 300 matches the Jackery 5000 Plus with roughly half the battery. These figures treat draw under a 40-50 W load as fan watts plus the no-load idle. That is an approximation: no named source measured an actual fan run.
